newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Eight killed in Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Eight killed in Karachi violence.

text.p: At least eight people died violently in Pakistan's industrial port city of Karachi during an Islamic religious holiday on Friday, police said on Saturday.
They said the bodies of the eight, including a political activist and a former policeman, were found in different places in the sprawling city.

However, police chief Mohib Asad of Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, told reporters that deaths from political and ethnic in the city had gone down over the past 15 days during which more than 2,000 people had been arrested in a crackdown on crime.
Violent feuding erupted in Karachi in recent weeks between militants of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and its splinter Haqiqi faction.
At least 175 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi so far this year compared to about 500 last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.
The MQM is a partner in Sindh province's coalition government, led by Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party.
